#Q2

```{r}
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)

```

```{r}
nhanes_covar = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
  skip = 4,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  rename(
    id = SEQN,
    bmi = BMI
  ) |>
  drop_na(sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )


nhanes_accel = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_accel.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  rename(id = SEQN)
```



```{r}
nhanes_joint_tidy = nhanes_covar |>
  inner_join(nhanes_accel, by = "id")

```

```{r}
nhanes_joint_tidy |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Education level", "Men", "Women"),
    caption = "Number of participants by education level and sex"
  )

```

```{r}
# Age distributions by sex and education
age_plot = nhanes_joint_tidy |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ education,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 20)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Age distributions by sex and education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

age_plot

```
The sample includes 228 participants. The more than high school category is the largest, with 56 men and 59 women. The less than high school category has nearly equal numbers of men and women (27 and 28), while the high school equivalent category includes more men than women (35 versus 23). Participants with more than a high school education tend to be younger, with median ages in the early 40s for both sexes. In the less than high school category, median ages are approximately 60 for both sexes. In the high school equivalent category, women tend to be older than men, with median ages of approximately 62 and 53, respectively.







```{r}
#Total daily activity for each participant 
nhanes_total = nhanes_joint_tidy |>
  mutate(
    total_activity = rowSums(pick(starts_with("min")))
  )

total_activity_plot = nhanes_total |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ education,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 20)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity and age",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily activity (summed MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

total_activity_plot
```
Total daily activity generally decreases with age across all education categories, although the smooth curves show nonlinear patterns. The decline is particularly clear in the less than high school category. In the high school equivalent category, activity peaks around ages 35–40 before declining, with women generally showing higher activity than men through much of middle age. Among participants with more than a high school education, women generally have higher activity than men until the curves converge near age 80. Considerable variation exists among participants of similar ages, and sex differences are less consistent in the less than high school category.





```{r}
nhanes_long = nhanes_joint_tidy |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    names_transform = list(minute = as.integer),
    values_to = "mims"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hour = (minute - 1) / 60
  )

```

```{r}
#Mean activity at each minute by education and sex

nhanes_timecourse = nhanes_long |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute, hour) |>
  summarize(
    mean_mims = mean(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

```{r}

#Activity over the 24-hour day 

timecourse_plot = nhanes_timecourse |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = mean_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(
    alpha = 0.25,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    formula = y ~ x,
    span = 0.15,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ education,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 20)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18, 24),
    labels = c("00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00", "24:00"),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average activity over the 24-hour day",
    subtitle = "Faint lines show minute-level means; bold lines show smooth trends",
    x = "Time of day",
    y = "Mean minute-level MIMS",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

timecourse_plot

```


All three education categories show a similar daily pattern: activity is lowest in the early morning, rises sharply around 06:00, remains elevated during the day, and declines in the evening. Participants with less than a high school education show a pronounced late-morning peak, with similar daytime activity between sexes but higher overnight activity among men. In the high school equivalent category, women generally show slightly higher activity during the late morning and early afternoon. The clearest daytime sex difference appears in the more than high school category, where women maintain higher activity through most of the day, particularly into the early evening. These descriptive differences may partly reflect differences in age composition across groups.





#Q3
```{r}

Jan_2020_Citi <- read_csv("data/Jan 2020 Citi.csv")


Jan_2024_Citi <- read_csv("data/Jan 2024 Citi.csv")


July_2020_Citi <- read_csv("data/July 2020 Citi.csv")


July_2024_Citi <- read_csv("data/July 2024 Citi.csv")

```

```{r}
citibike_tidy = bind_rows(
  "2020_January" = Jan_2020_Citi,
  "2024_January" = Jan_2024_Citi,
  "2020_July" = July_2020_Citi,
  "2024_July" = July_2024_Citi,
  .id = "source"
) |>
  separate(
    source,
    into = c("year", "month"),
    sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(
      year,
      levels = c("2020", "2024")
    ),
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c("January", "July")
    ),
    weekdays = str_to_title(str_trim(weekdays)),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c(
        "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
        "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
      )
    ),
    member_casual = factor(
      str_to_lower(str_trim(member_casual)),
      levels = c("casual", "member"),
      labels = c("Casual", "Member")
    ),
    rideable_type = factor(
      str_to_lower(str_trim(rideable_type))
    ),
    across(
      c(start_station_name, end_station_name),
      ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), "")
    )
  )

glimpse(citibike_tidy)

```
```{r}
citibike_summary = citibike_tidy |>
  summarize(
    n_rides = n(),
    n_variables = ncol(citibike_tidy),
    n_unique_ride_ids = n_distinct(ride_id),
    missing_start_station = sum(is.na(start_station_name)),
    missing_end_station = sum(is.na(end_station_name)),
    missing_duration = sum(is.na(duration)),
    missing_weekday = sum(is.na(weekdays)),
    missing_membership = sum(is.na(member_casual))
  )

citibike_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Summary of the combined Citi Bike dataset"
  )


citibike_tidy |>
  count(rideable_type)

summary(citibike_tidy$duration)

```


The cleaned dataset contains 99,485 rides and 9 variables, combining January and July data from 2020 and 2024. Each row represents a unique ride and includes its ID, bike type, weekday, duration, starting and ending stations, membership status, year, and month. There are 55,536 classic bike rides and 43,949 electric bike rides. Starting station names are missing for 43 rides, and ending station names are missing for 207 rides; these records are retained for analyses that do not require station information. Ride duration, weekday, and membership status have no missing values. Ride durations are right-skewed, with a median of 9.84 and a mean of 13.93, ranging from approximately 1.00 to 238.78.



```{r}
ride_count_table = citibike_tidy |>
  count(year, month, member_casual, name = "n_rides") |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n_rides,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Total = Casual + Member
  ) |>
  arrange(year, month)

ride_count_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Casual", "Member", "Total"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Number of sampled rides by year, month, and membership"
  )

```


Members account for most sampled rides in every year–month combination. July has more rides than January in both years, and both casual and member ride counts are higher in 2024 than in the corresponding months of 2020. July 2024 has the largest total, with 47,156 rides, compared with 21,048 in July 2020. Casual riders also represent a larger share of rides in July than in January: approximately 27% versus 8% in 2020 and 23% versus 11% in 2024. These results suggest seasonal differences in ridership and increased system use between the two years.









```{r}
top_start_stations = citibike_tidy |>
  filter(
    year == "2024",
    month == "July",
    !is.na(start_station_name)
  ) |>
  count(start_station_name, name = "n_rides") |>
  arrange(desc(n_rides), start_station_name) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

top_start_stations |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Starting station", "Number of rides"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Five most popular starting stations in July 2024"
  )
```



```{r}
median_duration = citibike_tidy |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

median_duration_plot = median_duration |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = weekdays,
      y = median_duration,
      color = month,
      group = month
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median ride duration by weekday, month, and year",
    x = "Day of the week",
    y = "Median ride duration",
    color = "Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

median_duration_plot

```
Median ride duration is higher in July than in January on every day of the week in both years. Durations are also consistently lower in 2024 than in 2020, with a particularly large decrease in July. In July 2020, median duration rises from approximately 13–14 on weekdays to 16.5 on weekends, compared with approximately 9–10 and 10.5–11, respectively, in July 2024. Weekend increases are also evident in January 2020, whereas January 2024 shows relatively little variation across the week and a decrease on Sunday. Overall, the July–January difference and the weekend increase are more pronounced in 2020.








```{r}
citibike_tidy |>
  filter(year == "2024") |>
  group_by(month, member_casual, rideable_type) |>
  summarize(
    n_rides = n(),
    median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(duration, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(duration, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Ride duration summaries in 2024"
  )
  
```


In 2024, casual riders have longer median ride durations and wider interquartile ranges than members within each month and bike type. Median durations are higher in July than in January across all groups. Among casual riders, classic bike rides last longer than electric bike rides, with medians of 15.62 versus 12.94 in July. Among members, electric bike rides have slightly higher medians than classic bike rides, particularly in July (9.24 versus 7.68). Casual classic bike rides show the greatest variability in both months. Overall, differences by membership status are more pronounced than differences by bike type.
